frozen_candidate_root_contribution: Directed, completive ARRIVAL AT A DESIGNATED TERMINUS: some entity — a person, event, message, thing, or conferred good — comes-to and REACHES a goal-point (a person, place, time, act, or state). Form I predicates the entity's own arrival at the goal; Form I + bi- and the causative Form IV (آتى / يؤتي) add an agent who makes an object arrive at a recipient, i.e. "bring / produce / hand-over / bestow / render-a-due." The invariant left in every token is the reaching-of-a-terminus (causatively: the making-reach).

internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The 549 tokens split by morphology into two branches that share one core. FORM I = intransitive arrival: "أَتَىٰ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ" the command of God has come (16:1); "أَتَىٰهَآ أَمْرُنَا" Our decree came to it (10:24); "فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا" when Moses came to the fire (20:11); "يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ" the day the punishment comes to them (14:44); "مَن يَأْتِ رَبَّهُۥ مُجْرِمًا" whoever comes to his Lord as a sinner (20:74); "هَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰ" has the account of Moses come to you (79:15); "أَتَتْ عَلَيْهِ" the wind comes upon it (51:42); "هَلْ أَتَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْإِنسَٰنِ حِينٌ" has a span of time come upon man (76:1). FORM I + bi- = bring/produce (cause-to-come-along): "فَأْتُوا۟ بِسُورَةٍ" bring a sura (10:38, 2:23); "ٱئْتُونِى بِهِۦ" bring him to me (12:50); "يَأْتِيكُم بِضِيَآءٍ" brings you light (28:71). FORM IV causative = give/bestow (make-arrive-at-recipient): "ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَٰبَ" We gave Moses the Book (2:53); "تُؤْتِى ٱلْمُلْكَ مَن تَشَآءُ" You give kingship to whom You will (3:26); "ءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ" give the zakat (2:43); "ءَاتُوا۟ ٱلنِّسَآءَ صَدُقَٰتِهِنَّ" give the women their dowries (4:4). The two branches are proven identical by the corpus itself: 2:258 uses Form I + bi for "God brings (يَأْتِى بِـ) the sun from the east; [you] bring (فَأْتِ بِـ) it from the west," and Form IV for "give"; 24:33 "وَءَاتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ ءَاتَىٰكُمْ" give them of God's wealth which He gave you; 59:7 "وَمَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ" whatever the Messenger brings/gives you, take it. Passive Form IV أُوتُوا = "made to have X come to them": "ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ" those given the Book (3:19); "مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ" whoever is given his record in his right hand (69:19). Participle/verbal-noun N: "ٱلسَّاعَةَ لَـَٔاتِيَةٌ" the Hour is surely coming (15:85, 20:15, 22:7); "كُلُّهُمْ ءَاتِيهِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَرْدًا" each will come to Him alone (19:95); "كَانَ وَعْدُهُۥ مَأْتِيًّا" His promise is one that will be arrived-at/fulfilled (19:61). N(IV) verbal noun: "إِيتَآءِ ٱلزَّكَوٰةِ" the giving of zakat (16:90, 21:73, 24:37). Idiomatic "come-unto/commit": "أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةَ" do you come-unto the abomination (7:80, 27:54); "يَأْتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةٍ" commit immorality (4:19); "لَا يَأْتُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ إِلَّا وَهُمْ كُسَالَىٰ" they do not come to prayer except lazily (9:54). Cosmic: "ٱئْتِيَا طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًا قَالَتَآ أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ" [heaven & earth] come willingly or unwillingly — they said, we come willingly (41:11). Every family reduces to arrival-at, or made-to-arrive-at, a terminus.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Subtract FORM: Form I = intransitive arrival (come / arrive / come-upon); Form IV آتى/يؤتي = causative "make-arrive-at-recipient" = give/bestow/render; إيتاء = the act of making-arrive (giving); آتٍ/آتية = arriving; مأتيّ = arrived-at/attained. Subtract CONSTRUCTION: bare object / ilā = come to; ʿalā = come upon (أتى على, 25:40, 51:42, 76:1); bi- = come-bringing = bring/produce; double object (IV) = give X to Y. Prepositions supply only the vector (to / upon / with); the arrival-at-terminus is constant. Subtract PARTICIPANTS: subject may be God, messengers, punishment, the Hour, a decree, the sun, news, food, water, gifts, or an evil act as goal; recipient may be people, God, a place, or an act. Subtract CONTEXT: eschatological (Hour/punishment arriving), legal (giving zakat/dowry/records), narrative (Moses reaching the fire), polemical (bring a sura like it). What remains in all 549 = the reaching-of / coming-to a terminus (causatively, the making-reach).
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The hardest tokens are Form IV bestowals of an inalienable, internal disposition, where any literal "coming/motion" is maximally bleached: 47:17:5 "وَءَاتَىٰهُمْ تَقْوَىٰهُمْ" (He gave them their piety) and 32:13:3 "لَـَٔاتَيْنَا كُلَّ نَفْسٍ هُدَىٰهَا" (We would have given every soul its guidance). Reconciliation: these are the identical double-object causative as "gave him the Book" (2:53) — the quality is made to accrue to / reach the recipient, who remains the terminus; the arrival residue here is grammatical (IV = transparent causative of أتى) rather than a felt physical motion, but it is directly corroborated by the corpus pairing Form I + bi "bring" with Form IV "give" for the very same referents (2:258 bring/give the sun; 24:33 "give of the wealth He gave you"; 59:7 "what the Messenger brings/gives you"). It reconciles without forcing. (A near-rival for the Form-I side, "بِمَآ أَتَوا۟" = what they have done/brought-about, 3:188, and "لَـَٔاتَوْهَا" = they would have committed it, 33:14, likewise reconcile as arrival-at/engagement-with an act.)
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Strongest alternative center: TRANSFER/CONFERRAL (giving to a recipient), with "come" read as the intransitive inchoative ("a thing arrives = gives itself"). Internal evidence arbitrates AGAINST making transfer the center: the large Form I usage has no transferred object and no owner-recipient — "أَتَىٰ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ" (16:1), "يَأْتِيهِمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ" (14:44), "أَتَتْكَ ءَايَٰتُنَا" (20:126) cannot be read as transfer — whereas every "give" token IS reducible to "cause-to-come-to-recipient." Since Form I (arrival) is morphologically basic and Form IV (give) is its transparent causative, the determinate direction is arrival → (causative) transfer, not the reverse. A weaker alternative — bare "motion/come" — under-describes the data: the terminus/goal is always in view (which is precisely why the root causativizes so readily into "deliver/bestow/render a due"); the residue is completive arrival-AT a terminus, not mere directed motion.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors: (1) ج ي أ jāʾa "come" — the closest; both mean "come" and both occur, sometimes side by side (7:129 "مِن قَبْلِ أَن تَأْتِيَنَا وَمِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا جِئْتَنَا"). Internal differentiator: only ا ت ي productively forms the causative "give/bestow" (آتى/يؤتي, ~275 tokens) and the "bring/produce" formula (ٱئْتِ بـ / فَأْتُوا۟ بِـ) — i.e. ا ت ي foregrounds a terminus/RECIPIENT capable of receiving, spanning arrival→delivery; جاء in this corpus stays intransitive-arrival (no "give" causative) and clusters on the accomplished advent of truth/messengers/Hour ("جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْحَقُّ"), while ا ت ي freely covers prospective/conditional arrival ("مِن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِىَ يَوْمٌ" 14:31; "إِنْ أَتَىٰكُمْ عَذَابُهُۥ" 10:50). (2) ن ز ل nazala "descend" — adds a from-above vector absent in ا ت ي, whose arrival is direction-neutral ("مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ/يَحْتَسِبُوا۟" 16:26, 59:2; "مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ/ٱلْمَغْرِبِ" 2:258). (3) أعطى aʿṭā "hand over/grant" — the give-competitor; the corpus uses أعطى for paying the jizya (9:29 "يُعْطُوا۟ ٱلْجِزْيَةَ") but آتى for rendering the divinely-owed due (زكاة/أجور/صدقات), marking آتى as "cause the due/gift to reach its rightful terminus, esp. from a superior/God." Falsifiability: the unity fails if any token shows ا ت ي denoting a static state, possession, or bare existence with NO reaching-of-a-terminus (no goal, recipient, or arrival). No such token occurs — even absolute "ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ" (20:60) entails arrival at the scene, and every bestowed abstraction has a recipient-terminus.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty residue — completive ARRIVAL AT A DESIGNATED TERMINUS — is recoverable in every one of the 549 tokens once form and construction are subtracted. Form I predicates the arrival directly (the Hour/decree/punishment/news comes; a person comes to a place, to God, or "comes-unto" an act). Form I + bi- and the causative Form IV predicate the making-arrive of an object at a recipient (bring / produce / give / bestow / render-a-due), including the passive أُوتُوا "those to whom X was made to come." The give-branch is not a separate meaning but the grammatical causative of the come-branch, and the corpus itself demonstrates the identity by pairing Form I + bi "bring" with Form IV "give" for the same referents (2:258 bring/give the sun; 24:33 "give of the wealth He gave you"; 59:7 "what the Messenger brings/gives you"). The hardest tokens — bestowal of inalienable qualities (47:17, 32:13) and the "commit/do" idiom (7:80, 3:188, 33:14) — reconcile as, respectively, causative delivery-to-a-recipient and arrival-at/engagement-with an act, with no forcing. Direction is determinate (arrival basic, transfer its causative), the residue is surface-recoverable throughout, and it is sharply separable from جاء (which does not causativize to "give" here) and from نزل (which adds descent). No confirmed occurrence contradicts the residue; hence PREFERRED at STRONG. The only concession to full transparency is that a minority of Form-IV abstract bestowals make the arrival component grammatically-inferred rather than physically-felt — but that inference is internally attested, not imported, so it does not weaken the disposition below STRONG.

adversarial_verification.notes: Read all 549 tokens (N=10, N(IV)=4, V=264, V(IV)=271 = 549; sums check). Adversarial sweep found NO genuine failing occurrence. Every family reduces to the invariant: Form I = the entity's own directed arrival at a terminus (person/place/time/act/state), Form I+bi- and Form IV آتى/يؤتي = an agent making an object arrive at a recipient (bring/produce/hand-over/bestow/render-due), passive أُوتُوا = made-to-have-X-reach-them, participle/N = coming/arrived-at (مَأْتِيًّا 19:61) / giving (إيتاء). Hardest cases and their resolutions: (1) the 'commit' idiom أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةَ / لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلرِّجَالَ / يَأْتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةٍ (7:80,27:54,7:81,4:19,29:29,60:12,33:30,65:1) carries the weight of 'perpetrate,' but إتيان-الأمر ('come-unto→do') is a real, attested extension of the arrival sense with the deed as terminus — declared by the candidate, not circular; this is the most stretched but surviving point. (2) Conferral of intangibles يُؤْتِى ٱلْحِكْمَةَ (2:269), ءَاتَىٰهُمْ تَقْوَىٰهُمْ (47:17), ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا — metaphorical transfer to a recipient-terminus, standard. (3) Eventive/absolute come-to-pass أَتَىٰ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ (16:1), يَوْمَ يَأْتِ (11:105), ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ (20:60) — terminus implicit but arrival is still the core. (4) Destructive أَتَى ٱللَّهُ بُنْيَٰنَهُم (16:26), أَتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ (59:2) — arrival-at-with-intent. HOMONYMY CHECK (decisive): the two contaminating homonyms — ألو (يَأْتَلِ 24:22) and أنى (يَأْنِ 57:16) — are NOT the tagged tokens; 24:22:8:1 tags يُؤْتُوٓا۟ 'give' and 57:16:17:1 tags أُوتُوا۟ 'given.' The tagged set contains no sense outside arrive/give, so there is no semantic split or homonymy to bridge. DISTINCTIVENESS: the come+causative-give bundle is not a vague blob. Its thinnest point is the intransitive branch's near-synonymy with جاء (both take عذاب/أمر/رسل/نبأ; cf. أَتَىٰ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ 16:1 vs جَآءَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ 11:76 in the same slot). But the root as a whole is sharply distinct from جاء (which has NO causative 'give' sense) and from أعطى/وهب (آتى frames giving as making-something-come/arrive, i.e., causative of the motion root). FALSIFIABILITY: any non-motion, non-transfer predicate would refute the invariant; none of the 549 meets that condition. The definition is broad (5 entity types x 5 terminus types) but this is the genuine, morphologically-conditioned polysemy of ا ت ي, not vacuous over-breadth — it still excludes all stationary predicates. Verdict SUPPORTED; failing_occurrences empty.
